title: Rabbi Acha bar Chanina
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: His father Rabbi Chanina is mentioned in Tanchuma, Naso 5: “Our Rabbis said in the name of Rabbi Chanina, the father of Rabbi Acha”; and there, Shelach 27: “So Rabbi Tanchuma bar Abba opened, in the name of Rabbi Chanina, the father of Rabbi Acha bar Chanina.” His mother was the sister of Shmuel bar Nachum, as in Bava Kamma 55a. Hyman infers from the father being identified through his son that the son was a leading sage of the generation.

Hyman suggests that his birthplace was Lod, and there he received the halakhot of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, as in Berakhot 8b, “Rabbi Acha son of Rabbi Chanina said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said”; there, 8a, he said on Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s words, “What is the verse?”; and in Chullin 132b, “When Rabbi Acha bar Chanina came from the South, he said in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.” He brought several baraitot from there, as we find, “When Rabbi Acha bar Chanina came from the South, he brought a baraita with him,” as in Sukkah 54a and Yevamot 57a and 58a. Hyman argues that he was not Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi’s student but received from his students, for he was Rabbi Assi’s student and received from him the halakhot of Rabbi Yochanan, as in Shabbat 45b, Sanhedrin 41b and 42a (several halakhot), Menachot 103a and the end of Shabbat, chapter 3 (there bar Chinena). He likewise received: “Rabbi Acha bar Chanina said that Abaye said that Rabbi Assi said” — Hyman proposes “Rabbi Abbahu said.” In Berakhot 5a he disagrees with Rabbi Yaakov bar Idi, and Rabbi Abba son of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said to them, “Thus said Rabbi Yochanan.” He likewise disagrees with Ulla, as in Rosh Hashanah 2a. Hyman emphasizes that he was so great that all the great Babylonian Amoraim raised difficulties from his halakhot, as in Chullin 132a, where Rav Nachman said to Rabbi Tavla, “But did not Rabbi Acha bar Chanina say?”; and in Eruvin 64a Rava said to Rav Yosef, “But did not Rabbi Acha bar Chanina say?” His precious homilies remain to us: Shabbat 55a, “Rabbi Zeira said in his name: Never did a good measure go forth from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, and He retracted it”; Pesachim 51a [supplied locator; see note], “Not like this world is the world to come,” etc.; Sanhedrin 47a, “From where do we know that one does not bury a wicked person next to a righteous one?” (and where they said there, “Rav Papa said to him,” Hyman proposes supplying “to Abaye”; in Chullin 6b it is correct that Rav Papa raised a difficulty against Abaye, and not against Rabbi Acha bar Chanina, who was in the Land of Israel); in Sanhedrin 81a his precious saying: “What is the meaning of what is written, ‘[He has not eaten] upon the mountains … and has not defiled his neighbor’s wife’ — that he did not encroach on his fellow’s trade; ‘and has not approached a menstruant woman’ — that he did not benefit from the charity fund”; and in Berakhot, chapter 2, end of halakhah 4, Rabbi Levi in his name: “Why did they place ‘Who blesses the years’ next to ‘Who gathers’?” etc. His sayings are likewise mentioned in Berakhot 8a and 51b, Shabbat 75b, Tanchuma, Bereshit 7, Noach 4 and Kedoshim 4, and Midrash Tehillim 15:29.

Seder HaDorot cites a saying of his from Menachot 32b, “If he changed in this and in that, it is invalid, and Rabbi Acha declares it valid”; Hyman says, with respect, that he erred in this, for there it is a baraita, and it is Rabbi Acha the Tanna, as they said there, “like the Tannaim.”

notes.text: The birthplace, teacher chronology, missing-to-Abaye emendation and distinction from Rabbi Acha the Tanna remain Hyman’s arguments. תלמודי is interpreted as תלמידו and כהונן as כהוגן. Hyman supplies Pesachim נא. (51a); the earlier draft’s 50a comparison is retained here as a comparison, without claiming a fresh Pesachim primary inspection in this review. The body now retains the supplied locator.

A fresh direct reading of Pesachim 50a names Acha bar Chanina and the saying contrasting this world’s blessings for good and bad news with the world to come. Hyman supplies 51a. The current note recording that the earlier review did not freshly inspect Pesachim is retained verbatim; this is an additional inspection, not a rewriting of that history. Sanhedrin 81a directly continues his homily with not entering a fellow’s trade and not benefiting from the charity fund. These witnesses do not independently establish Hyman’s Lod origin, leading-generation inference, teacher chronology, proposed Abaye-to-Abbahu substitution, or missing-to-Abaye emendation. His distinction from the Tanna Acha remains attributed.
